claims.claim: Compton says the most common way generators fail is producing content that fails to be interesting.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: generators fail is that they produce content that fails to be interesting

claims.feature: other: uneven salience as a cure
claims.claim: Compton proposes that most generated artifacts can be drab background noise so that a few characterful artifacts stand out.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016

claims.claim: Compton defines a generator's possibility space as all the kinds of artifacts it can generate.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: all the kinds of artifacts it can generate
claims.page: section on constraints and desirable properties

claims.claim: Compton says that when bad content cannot be defined it becomes impossible to filter.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016

claims.feature: other: elicit the human process first
claims.claim: Compton advises sitting with a practitioner and recording the questions they ask themselves while making the artifact, as the basis for a generator.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: What questions do they ask themselves along the way?

claims.claim: Compton cites Kevin Lynch's 'Image of the City' for the claim that there are factors that make cities memorable and describable, and suggests other such aesthetic rules may be discoverable.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: there are factors that make cities memorable and describable

claims.feature: other: mechanical connection as the cure
claims.claim: Emily Short says the key question in avoiding procedural oatmeal is whether the generation is connected to anything mechanical.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: whether the generation is connected to anything mechanical

claims.claim: Emily Short says generated names and text are purely decorative unless tightly correlated with gameplay.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: purely decorative unless it is tightly correlated with gameplay

claims.claim: Emily Short says the player will soon realize decorative generated text is decorative and start looking past it.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: realize that it is decorative and start looking past it

claims.feature: other: generation is not a content shortcut
claims.claim: Emily Short says procedural generation is not a substitute for designing content but a way of designing content.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016

claims.claim: Emily Short says procedural generation is often at least as labor-intensive as other ways of designing content.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: at least as labor-intensive as other ways

claims.claim: Emily Short says procedural methods are good at low-level layered consequence, representing how the player has changed the world state persistently in a small way.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: representing how the player has changed the world state persistently

claims.claim: A reader commenting as 'Dryman' frames the oatmeal problem as the difficulty of making generated differences matter to an audience, and Short answers that comment in the post.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: hard to make these differences *matter* to an audience
claims.page: opening block quote of the reader comment

claims.feature: other: generated text as status information
claims.claim: Emily Short says she wanted everything the robot in The Mary Jane of Tomorrow said to act as a reminder of her current training state.
claims.source: Emily Short, 'Bowls of Oatmeal and Text Generation', emshort.blog, 21 Sep 2016
claims.quote: a reminder of her current training state
claims.page: body, paragraph on The Mary Jane of Tomorrow

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead say a generator that makes tens of thousands of levels quickly is useless if many of those levels are effectively identical to each other.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: many of those levels are effectively identical to each other
